propositions: Build and test a committed operational script that uses stock Git plumbing (fast-export/fast-import) to rewrite repository history, stripping .bridge_state/ and .bridge_state.bak-retarget/ prefixes from all commits while preserving DAG topology and merge structure.

The dry-run script must refuse execution on partial (blob:none) clones and require a fresh unfiltered clone, then prove commit/merge-commit counts match, tree byte-identically matches old tip after dynamic re-add, target history is absent except at rewritten HEAD, and source remote refs remain unchanged.

The script must parse fast-export data blocks by byte length rather than line-based filtering to correctly handle commit messages that begin with command-like bytes (M or D), and dynamically derive the re-add file set from git ls-tree to remain safe for future .bridge_state/ extensions.

The dry-run produces a rewritten branch with pack size at most 150 MB and asserts that the protected remote tag refs/tags/pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z is absent locally before pack measurement and unchanged on source remote; the script never performs any push operation.

Validation proves the rewritten history via unit tests for binary framing (adversarial messages), integration tests for graph/tree/tag/pack assertions on real repositories, and a representative post-rewrite writer push showing old tip is not an ancestor and incremental pack grows less than 1 MB.

After dry-run completion, all graph, tree, history-removal, and pack-size assertions must complete before the script emits its final success result; any assertion failure exits nonzero and recovery restarts from a fresh unfiltered clone.
